question.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}0 & 2 \\ 6 & -6\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}],\,y=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Given the matrices above, write the following expression as a Hadamard product. Here $(\,\cdot \,)$ denotes matrix multiplication.

| $(AB)\cdot (By)=\,\,$ |  | {{field-1}} |  | $⊙$ |  | {{field-2}} |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
|  | $-6$ |  |  | $4$ |  |  |  |  |
question.worked_solution:
The Hadamard product of two compatible vectors $u$ and $v$ can be expressed as the matrix product

$$
v⊙u=\text{diag}(v)u.
$$

In our case, we have

$$
AB=[\begin{aligned}0 & 2 \\ 6 & -6\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & -6\end{aligned}]
$$

and

$$
By=[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}4 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 4\end{aligned}].
$$

Hence, 

$$
\begin{aligned}(AB)\cdot (By) & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & -6\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}3 \\ 4\end{aligned}] \\  & =\text{diag}([\begin{aligned}2 \\ -6\end{aligned}])[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 4\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -6\end{aligned}]⊙[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 4\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
